## About
My life in wheel alignment started at a chain shop. After years of slowly gathering equipment and building a client base, I opened a little shop of my own. Today you'll find me in Hopkins.
I use a Hunter alignment computer and have been to several Hunter advanced training workshops, but I can also put a vehicle straight with hand tools. My pricing is set similar to the chain shops, without the pressure to rush and cut corners. As Miracle Max said: "You rush a miracle man, you get rotten miracles."
I work alone, so all work is by appointment and I tend to be booked a few days to a week out. Be on time, don't block the shop door, and you'll get "Happy Jeff." I may growl and bark, but I've never actually bitten anyone.

## Services
- Computerized wheel alignments: Alignments on a Hunter camera system, set to factory specs or your own custom settings.
- Tire service: Mounting with a Hunter tulip style changer with plastic tool surfaces, plus some tire sales. Bring tires you bought by mail order.
- Wheel balancing: Computer balancing with finger plates for better centering, and a wide range of wheel weights kept in stock.
- Suspension and steering parts: Struts, ball joints, tie rod ends, drive axles and other bushing and bearing press work.
- Brake work: Brake relines and rotor and drum machining. ABS service is not offered right now.
- Corner weight adjustments: Corner weighting for street and track cars using digital scales.
- Some motorcycle work: Limited motorcycle tire work using the Hunter machine and a static balancer.

## FAQ
Q: Do I need an appointment?
A: Yes. Jeff works alone, so every job is booked ahead to keep wait times short.

Q: How far out is Jeff booked?
A: Usually a few days to a week, so reach out ahead of time.

Q: Can I bring tires I bought online?
A: Yes. Mail order buyers are welcome.

Q: Do you do ABS service?
A: Not at this time. Jeff doesn't own a scan tool, so ABS work is off the menu for now.
